As for a powerful local-model rival to 5.5, I have no idea. Iirc the latest Qwen models come close to 4.8 or something. But I don't have a new/beefy enough build to try out anything supposedly groundbreaking.

comments.author: Old-Wolverine-4134
comments.body: To run such model locally you would need 3-4 TERABYTES of VRAM. The current local models are not even close to anything Opus 5.5 can do. Also reverse engineering games consumes a lot of usage - therefore it is not free and it cost much more than 5 bucks....

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body:
you can run Qwen 3.8 Flash-Next on Strata with varying results (depending how much RAM and VRAM you have), but I swing it with an RTX 3090 and 96GB of RAM and it is very impressive for a local model, (I hear it outperforms Qwen-3.8 27B, which is the other local workhorse model). You could run it on less hardware. Check out their requirements at [https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata)

You're not getting Opus 5.5 locally (*yet*). It's a multilingual expert across domains - you CAN get a local coding expert, though.

comments.author: Significant_Swim8994
comments.body:
I'm trying to develop something that might somehow compete, but it's still far off from actually working.

Feel free to follow my attempts, when I get around to having my local AI actually handle my projects. I'm currently "stuck" with SOL 6.1 on Codex, but also happy with the work it does!

I still havent found a single local AI with enough pondus or intelligence to take over at speeds that make sense, on the hardware I have available (my machine is just a 32GB RAM + 4070ti with 12 GB VRAM).

But the plan is to use multiple machines running/auto-changing between a vast library of different models depending on the tasks at hand. Auto-adjusting to use the models best rated for the task and using the connected hardware that has proven itself to best run the different models. Always adapting, auto-testing new models when the framework otherwise is not in use. Always adapting and learning from the work done.

I steal with arms and legs from any publicly available code and ideas to build out my idea. I dont even know how many different methods and concepts and ideas have been packed into the framework, but it should select and use the best amalgams of ideas for the task at hand, so it doesn't always just use the same model and method for all work.

Nothing is holy as long as its open source and freely available!

[Agnostic.dk - Projects - Workbench Compute Fabric](https://agnostic.dk/projects/compute-fabric/)

I might release it, once it works, I might not. I dont know; if it works well, it might become a paid product, but I'm not a greedy person, so I hope I retain that feeling, if I decide to put a price on it.

But you can read about it and some basic forms of my ideas and maybe find inspiration to build your own.

Warning: AI auto-summarizes the ideas into every short form and auto-builds/-updates the website, and I'm too lazy to cleanly (re)write it in more human language.

Live with it!
